work.text: Huang Zijiu’s [Huang Gongwang’s] River and Mountains on a Clear Autumn Day looks like this. I truly regret that this ancient master has not seen my work.

source.author: Dong Qichang
source.title: Inscription on the painting
source.publisher: translation in the Cleveland Museum of Art collection record

work.text: Here, Dong places an abstract landscape composition diagonally across the picture plane, configured to recall earlier masters and simultaneously express his own personal style.

moment.text: Dong Qichang had a tremendous impact on the artistic practices and historiography of later generations; his works and writings shaped literati aesthetics.
In fact, Dong Qichang may have had Dong Yuan’s Xiao and Xiang Rivers in mind, a work he owned and considered a key work in Chinese art history.

matters.text: Each time Dong Qichang encountered the mirror-smooth Korean paper, his calligraphy and painting became even more inspired. Here in this scroll he made use of a paper that formerly was meant for tributary presentation. One can still discern faint traces of written characters.

matters.text: Since Mr. Mantang does not own any handscrolls by Wenmin [Dong Qichang], I leave this one for him in commemoration of our parting; thus the painting will have a worthy owner and our meeting will become a beautiful story in the future.
